summary: Build a Python FastAPI service that receives GitHub pull request webhooks and runs a centralized LangGraph SDLC workflow with BA, developer, tester, documentation, and auditor roles.

workspaceSignals.decisionReason: LangGraph-sdlc is a new project folder; the parent exercise provides LangGraph and Python conventions but no existing application service to augment.

questions.question: Which programming language for SDLC Automation API?

options.label: Python
options.description: Use the existing LangGraph exercise's Python ecosystem and typing conventions.

questions.rationale: The requirements explicitly name LangGraph in Python, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, and PyGithub, and the parent exercise is a Python LangGraph project.

questions.question: Which framework approach for SDLC Automation API?

options.label: FastAPI + LangGraph
options.description: Expose GitHub webhook endpoints through FastAPI and orchestrate agent nodes with LangGraph.

questions.rationale: The supplied requirements specify a centralized FastAPI backend and a unified LangGraph state graph.

questions.question: Describe the features or API routes for SDLC Automation API.
questions.recommendedChoice: POST /webhook/github for pull_request events; fetch repository and diff context with PyGithub; run BA analysis, developer review, tester analysis, documentation generation, and structured audit nodes in a bounded LangGraph workflow; retry or revise documentation up to three times; post the final Markdown result back to the pull request; expose GET /health for operational checks.
questions.answer: POST /webhook/github for pull_request events; fetch repository and diff context with PyGithub; run BA analysis, developer review, tester analysis, documentation generation, and structured audit nodes in a bounded LangGraph workflow; retry or revise documentation up to three times; post the final Markdown result back to the pull request; expose GET /health for operational checks.
questions.rationale: The supplied SDLC multi-agent requirements define the webhook, GitHub integration, documentation/audit loop, and LangGraph state; the additional roles are the requested practical initial scope.

questions.question: Which data stores does your app need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Keep workflow state in the LangGraph invocation and use GitHub as the source of repository and pull request data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Persist generated documents or repository artifacts outside GitHub.

options.label: Queue Storage
options.description: Buffer webhook work for asynchronous processing.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Persist workflow runs, audit history, and operational metadata.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Persist relational workflow data in Azure SQL.

questions.rationale: The initial requirements describe an event-triggered workflow that can keep state in one LangGraph run and post results to GitHub; durable run history and queueing are deferred.

questions.question: Does this app need user login?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Add user sign-in for application API access.

options.label: No
options.description: No user-facing sign-in is needed for the webhook service.

questions.rationale: The service is triggered by GitHub webhooks and does not specify a user-facing application login flow.
